Subject: POC trial environment: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC — next steps

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps for the POC/trial: 

1) Success criteria (as discussed)
- Latency: 95th percentile < 350ms for single-turn generation at your typical prompt lengths
- Throughput: support sustained 50 req/s across peak slices
- Cost: target unit cost < $0.005/token (baseline to measure against)
- Functional: responses must meet the Category A accuracy threshold on your 200 test prompts

2) Evaluation plan
- Week 0: provisioning and access; baseline tests against sample workloads
- Week 1: run evaluation suite (200 prompts + 10k token workload); capture latency/cost/quality
- Week 2: iterate on config (batching, quantization, model variant) and re-evaluate
- End of Week 3: final report and go/no-go decision

3) Environment options (high level)
- Hosted (fastest): Hosted API sandbox on Redwood — quickest to start (hours), lowest setup friction. Good for functional/latency checks.
- Dedicated sandbox: reserved GPU pool for your account (predictable throughput, performs closest to production) — provisioning ~4–6 weeks.
- VPC/private deployment: customer VPC with private network peering and KMS integration — required if you need strict data residency/network controls; provisioning typically 2–3 weeks for initial network review, longer for on-prem.

4) Recommended plan (based on our conversation):
- Kick off with a 2–3 week hosted trial to validate functional quality and baseline latency/cost.
- If you need isolated throughput or stricter controls after baseline, move to a dedicated sandbox for performance tuning.
- Pursue VPC only if your security/compliance requires private networking or on-prem controls.

5) Ownership & next steps
- Marissa Cole (Redwood): program owner — schedule kickoff, coordinate timelines, collect success metrics.
- Vivek Kulkarni (Redwood): technical onboarding and network checklist owner.
- Lauren Bishop (Redwood): contract/SLA & procurement contact.
- Alyssa / Mike (Acme AI): provide sample prompt sets, representative traffic profile, and network contacts for VPC review.

Attachments: redwood-poc-mpa.pdf (POC scope & success metrics), acme-network-checklist.xlsx (network intake)

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Please confirm you want to start with Hosted trial (we can provision sandbox and share credentials within 24 hours).
- Share the sample prompts and a short CSV of traffic shape (QPS distribution by hour).
- Suggest kickoff call next week to align stakeholders and run through the evaluation checklist.

Thanks — happy to adjust based on priorities.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Alyssa — great questions, answered inline below and with a recommended plan: 

1) Hosted trial — residency
- We can provision hosted sandboxes in specific regions (us-west, us-east, eu-west) and we do not replicate logs across regions by default. For EU data you can request eu-west region; we will ensure data at rest is contained and tokens are not exported to third-party analytics. For compliance-critical work we recommend VPC/private deployment.

2) Dedicated sandbox timeline
- Standard timeline is 4–6 weeks for a reserved environment (procurement + infra). We have an accelerated path: with a signed short-term commit and an intake completed within 48 hours, we can often push to 2–3 weeks. Lauren will handle the paperwork.

3) VPC network prerequisites
- Minimum: allowlist of static egress IPs (we'll provide ranges), open outbound ports 443 and 5223 for control plane, an IPsec or AWS PrivateLink option for private connectivity. We capture detailed items in the attached acme-network-checklist.xlsx. Vivek will run a short tech call with Mike to validate.

Recommended immediate plan:
- Start with Hosted trial in eu-west (per your EU needs) — Marissa to provision and share creds within 24 hrs after you confirm.
- Parallel: Vivek to run quick network 30-min call with Mike to validate if VPC will be needed. If not needed, proceed through Hosted and Dedicated as next step.
- Lauren to prepare a short-term reserved offer (optional) if you want to accelerate to Dedicated after baseline.

I’ve attached an updated POC plan and the network checklist. Intake form + scheduling link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-poc
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/ACME-77

Marissa

HI team — quick technical clarifications from my side to make the network call efficient: 

- Expected request profile: baseline 10–20 req/s, peak spikes to 50 req/s (bursts short-lived). For Hosted, we suggest testing with a ramp to 60 req/s to validate headroom.
- Tokenization: please confirm avg prompt length and avg completion length; tune max_tokens per request to avoid unintended cost.
- IP ranges: we will provide a short allowlist file (3 contiguous /24s) — acme-network-checklist.xlsx includes the exact CIDR ranges and sample firewall rules.
- TLS & certs: standard TLS; we support mTLS for VPC-based connections if your infra requires it.

Action items for Mike (cc’d via Alyssa):
- Share representative JMeter or k6 script (or a CSV of QPS by minute) so I can pre-wire test harness in the sandbox.
- Confirm whether your corp firewall allows outbound to our control-plane IPs and that you have a point of contact for peering.

I’ll join the tech call — suggest Tue 9/7 or Wed 9/8 morning PT.

Thanks,
